newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila grains buyers sidelined by peso woes.
newsitem.headline: Manila grains buyers sidelined by peso woes.

text.p: Manila grains buyers are expected to sit out of the market this week as they wait for the peso to steady, traders said on Monday.
Manila wheat buyers would also be sidelined because they were waiting for prices to soften.
Traders said U.S. wheat prices were still at high levels due to fears of a drought in some countries in Asia-Pacific, particularly China.
"Even if U.S. wheat will slide, we are still saddled by a higher peso," said an executive in a Philippine mill.
The peso has fallen more than nine percent against the dollar since July 11 when the Central Bank released its grip on the currency in the face of relentless speculative attacks.
The peso opened at 29 on Monday compared to 26.40 before its de-facto devaluation.
Last week, two Philippine flour mills bought 100,000 tonnes Canadian wheat for shipment between August and October.
"It was agreed that the price of the wheat will be determined just before the shipping date," said one trader close to the deal.
On corn and rice, the government and private firms are still considering possible effects of an expected dry spell due to the El Nino phenomenon.

Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said the state-owned National Food Authority has a "standby authority" to import 350,000 tonnes of rice - enough to meet the country's requirement for 15 days in case of emergency.
An agriculture expert recommended last month that the government book early rice imports for delivery in the first half of 1998 due to threats of a drought due to El Nino.
